claim: Phase 1 introduces `PartRefKey`, the three-value `Freshness` policy, an immutable index-free `PartFolderView`, `Store::readManifestShared`, strict manifest path ordering, and pure view-based post-resolve logic without a facade or retention.
Decoded `PartManifest::entries` must be strictly ascending by `path`; binary search and all index-free folder-view queries rely on this invariant.
`decodePartManifest` rejects an entry whose path is less than or equal to the preceding path with `CORRUPTED_DATA`, thereby rejecting out-of-order entries and non-adjacent duplicate paths.
`Cas::findEntry` performs binary search over decoded manifest entries and returns a pointer into the input vector or `nullptr` when the exact path is absent.
`Cas::entryRange` returns the contiguous `[first,last)` span of entries whose paths start with a directory prefix, and an empty prefix denotes the whole entry span.

`Store::readManifestShared` has the same mandatory `HEAD`, fail-closed `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST` and `CORRUPTED_DATA` behavior, and manifest-cache insertion semantics as `readManifest`, but returns the cached `std::shared_ptr<const PartManifest>` without a per-call copy.
`readManifest` remains a by-value compatibility shim over `readManifestShared` for callers that still require a value.
`PartRefKey` identifies a committed part or projection folder by owning root namespace plus ref name, where the ref is either a part name or the folded `detached/<part>` name.
`PartRefKey::cacheKey` joins namespace and ref with a NUL separator because NUL cannot occur in disk-derived namespace strings or ref names, making keys unambiguous even when refs contain `/`.

`Freshness::CachedForLoad` uses stale-tolerant ref resolution, `Freshness::ForceFresh` uses fresh resolution for mutable and write-source paths, and `Freshness::StrictValidate` bypasses retained views for fresh validated reads.

`PartFolderView` is an immutable no-I/O snapshot containing a resolved ref, copied mutable files, and the same `shared_ptr<const PartManifest>` held by the store manifest cache; mutable refreshes create a new view sharing that manifest pointer.
`PartFolderView` filters mutable names beginning with `.ca_` from user-visible file and directory answers.

`PartFolderView::projectionDirPrefix` recognizes a projection directory when its last path component ends in `.proj` or `.tmp_proj`, returning the routed file path with a trailing slash; other paths return no prefix.
`PartFolderView::fileSize` reports mutable value length, inline byte length, or blob size according to the matching file representation; `inlineBytes` returns bytes only for inline entries.
`PartFolderView::listChildren` collapses the first path component over manifest entries and non-reserved mutable files, including projection-directory listings.
`PartFolderView::estimatedBytes` conservatively includes fixed overhead, mutable key/value payload sizes, and `manifest_size`, intentionally over-counting the shared manifest decode.

Phase 1 changes `resolveRouted` to return an immutable `PartFolderView`, returning `nullptr` for an absent ref and surfacing missing or corrupt live manifests as exceptions rather than substituting a result.
For blob storage objects, the stored object length is the payload length, while `getBlobViewPlan` applies the blob header offset and file window for byte reads.

Phase 1 acceptance requires O(log n) manifest lookups, no per-operation manifest copies on the wiring read path, strict rejection of out-of-order bodies, and green `Cas*` tests with behavior preserved.

Phase 2 makes `CachedPartFolderAccess` the owner of freshness policy and terminal committed-ref primitives while `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage` retains path semantics and transactions retain staging orchestration.

`ContentAddressedMetadataStorage::partAccess` returns a reference so normal committed-ref mutations use dot syntax; raw `->dropRef`, `->updateRefPayload`, `->dropNamespace`, and `->promote` calls are forbidden in wiring outside `CachedPartFolderAccess`.
In Phase 2, `getView` always calls `readManifestShared`, including `CachedForLoad`, `ForceFresh`, and `StrictValidate`; there is no retained view state yet.
The facade read API consists of `getView`, `resolve`, and `existsRef`; `getView` returns `nullptr` for an absent ref, while `resolve` performs ref-only access without reading a manifest.
`CachedPartFolderAccess::dropRefIfPresent` treats an absent ref and a concurrent `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST` race as successful no-ops, while propagating other exceptions.
`CachedPartFolderAccess::dropRefBestEffort` is `noexcept`, swallows cleanup failures, and relies on garbage collection to reclaim lingering debris.

Phase 2 overrides `getStorageObjectsIfExist` to use one routed lookup for in-part paths, fixes `getFileSize` to use one routed resolve, and fixes `existsFileOrDirectory` to use one view query for committed in-part paths.
`CachedPartFolderAccess::publishEntries` performs `startBuild`, `adoptEvidence` for every entry, `stageManifest`, `precommitAdd`, and `promoteBuild` as the shared committed-publish sequence.
`republishRef` moves a committed source by publishing a fresh destination manifest and then dropping the source; an absent source returns `false` without writing.

An idempotent `republishRef` re-drive compares destination and source manifest entries, re-syncs destination mutable files when needed, and drops the source only when content matches; differing content raises `ABORTED` and leaves the source intact.
`adoptPartFromManifest` is consolidated onto `publishEntries`; sender identity is non-authoritative, while decoded entries are adopted as tokenless write evidence and re-proved during promotion.
After Phase 2 migration, `Cas::Store` is protocol-only: `Store::lookupPath` and the manifest overload of `Store::listDirectory` are deleted in favor of `Cas::findEntry` and `Cas::entryRange`.
The Phase 2 style guard is a best-effort textual check that rejects raw committed-ref mutation tokens in wiring files while exempting `Core/` and `CachedPartFolderAccess.*`.

Phase 3 registers eight `ProfileEvents`: `CasPartFolderViewHits`, `CasPartFolderViewMutableRefreshes`, `CasPartFolderViewValidationMismatches`, `CasPartFolderViewMisses`, `CasPartFolderViewEvictions`, `CasPartFolderViewOversizedBypasses`, `CasPartFolderViewInvalidations`, and `CasPartFolderManifestGets`.
Phase 3 registers `CurrentMetrics::CasPartFolderCacheBytes` and `CurrentMetrics::CasPartFolderCacheEntries` for retained view-cache size and entry count.
`CasPartFolderManifestGets` is incremented at the successful manifest body `GET` inside `Store::readManifestShared`, because the facade cannot distinguish a decode-cache hit from a body read.

The facade `explain` surface is bounded test/log-only state with decisions such as hit, mutable refresh, mismatch, miss, oversized bypass, strict bypass, force-fresh read, and invalidation; it has no SQL surface.
With retention disabled, five repeated `CachedForLoad` view builds perform one manifest body `GET` because the decode cache absorbs repeats and perform five mandatory manifest `HEAD`s.
The retained part-folder view cache defaults to 64 MiB, `cas_part_folder_cache_max_entries` defaults to 10000, and `cas_part_folder_cache_max_entry_bytes` defaults to 16 MiB.
`cas_part_folder_cache_bytes = 0` disables retained view caching and is a supported permanent operational configuration.
The retained view map is a byte-weighted `Common/CacheBase` LRU keyed by `PartRefKey::cacheKey`; it is consulted and populated only for `CachedForLoad`.

Every retained-view hit first re-resolves the ref and validates equality of `(manifest_id, mutable_files)`; an exact match returns the view without a manifest operation, a mutable-only mismatch clones around the same decode, and a manifest mismatch rebuilds the view.

`ForceFresh` and `StrictValidate` never serve a retained view; `ForceFresh` re-proves the manifest body through `readManifestShared` on every call, while `StrictValidate` also never retains the result.

The single-flight map coalesces concurrent cold `CachedForLoad` builds per `PartRefKey` through a shared future; its mutex is not held across ref resolution, manifest reads, or decoding, and leader failures propagate to followers.
Missing refs and failed view builds are never cached; views above `cas_part_folder_cache_max_entry_bytes` are served but bypass retention.
Write-through erases are cache hygiene rather than a correctness dependency; `dropRefBestEffort` erases even when its underlying drop fails because durable ref state is then unknown.
`dropNamespace` removes retained views whose canonical cache keys start with the namespace plus the NUL separator and increments the invalidation metric.
After a retained view is refreshed solely because `mutable_files` drifted while `manifest_id` stayed equal, no manifest `HEAD` or `GET` is required.

Phase 4 soak validation compares one CA-local plus CA-S3 run with retention enabled against one run with `cas_part_folder_cache_bytes = 0`, including anomaly baselines and `CasPartFolderView*` counters.
Phase 5 replaces the count-only manifest decode cache with a byte-weighted `CacheBase` LRU while leaving `shard_decode_cache` and `dedup_cache` in `Cas::Store`.

`manifest_decode_cache_bytes` defaults to 128 MiB and `0` disables manifest decode caching; the existing manifest-cache key remains `(ManifestId, Token)` so token changes force a miss and fresh decode.

The manifest decode-cache weight includes fixed overhead plus each entry's path size, inline-byte size, and per-entry overhead, and the view cache keeps its conservative `manifest_size` component because a view can outlive a decode-cache entry.
The approved 2026-07-08 design spec supersedes the RFC's open questions; the RFC remains motivation and context, while the spec is normative.

The design scope is content-addressed metadata reads and committed part-ref mutations below `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage`; it excludes `MergeTree` changes, `IMetadataStorage` API changes, and disk or pool format changes.

The architecture places one `CachedPartFolderAccess` facade between `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage` or `ContentAddressedTransaction` and `Cas::Store`; the facade serves immutable `PartFolderView` snapshots and owns committed part-ref mutations.

Validate-on-hit retention compares every retained view with a fresh `resolveRef` result using `(manifest_id, mutable_files)`; ref-staleness semantics therefore match existing behavior without relying on complete mutation-site invalidation coverage.

`readManifestShared` exposes the immutable manifest decode already held by `manifest_cache`, and strict decoder path ordering enables `PartFolderView` binary search and range scans without materialized indexes.

The two-level write API puts terminal committed-ref primitives and `republishRef` in the facade, while `publishEntries` replaces the near-duplicate publish body of `adoptPartFromManifest` and transaction staging remains in the transaction.
Phase 5 byte-bounds `manifest_cache` without relocating `shard_decode_cache` or `dedup_cache`, and retains the conservative `manifest_size` over-count in the view cache.

With retention disabled, answers and the read call graph remain identical to the existing behavior; with retention enabled, only manifest-body liveness validation on validated `CachedForLoad` hits is deferred.

The design does not cache blob payload bytes, ref absence, or namespace listings, and it does not add a disk-persistent cache, distributed invalidation, generic path-result cache, SQL introspection, or `IMetadataStorage` API.

Before the redesign, `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage` repeated route, ref resolution, manifest read, and path lookup across seven read methods; `readManifest` copied the cached manifest by value and performed a manifest-key `HEAD` on every call.

Before the redesign, `Store::lookupPath` and the manifest overload of `Store::listDirectory` were linear scans, while the encoder sorted entries but the decoder checked only adjacent duplicates and did not enforce ordering.
`resolveRef(allow_stale=true)` is bounded by `shard_decode_cache_ttl_ms` and locally write-coherent because committed shard mutations erase the shard decode-cache entry and bump `shard_write_seq`.

`ContentAddressedMetadataStorage` owns one facade instance, constructs it after `Store::open` during startup, resets it before `cas_store` during shutdown, and its accessor throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` before startup.
`PartFolderView` never calls back into metadata storage, never mutates `Cas::Store`, and performs no object-store I/O; `Cas::Store` does not depend on the facade.

`Freshness::CachedForLoad` resolves with `allow_stale=true` and may serve or retain a validated view; `ForceFresh` resolves with `allow_stale=false`, never serves a retained view, and may update a view after body validation; `StrictValidate` resolves fresh, never serves a retained view, and never retains a result.
Mutable per-part answers always come from the freshly resolved `Resolved::mutable_files`, never from an unvalidated retained view.

`PartFolderView` contains `PartRefKey`, `ManifestId`, encoded manifest size, publication time, copied mutable files, and the shared immutable manifest pointer; its query surface is pure and index-free.

The facade's committed-ref write API includes `promoteBuild`, `publishEntries`, `republishRef`, `updateMutableFiles`, `dropRef`, `dropRefIfPresent`, `dropRefBestEffort`, and `dropNamespace`; pass-through operations such as `listRefs`, `listNamespaces`, `listMirroredChildren`, namespace files, mountpoint objects, and `locate` remain on `Cas::Store`.

The normative `getView` algorithm first resolves the ref, returns `nullptr` for absence without retaining it, validates a retained view for `CachedForLoad`, builds through `readManifestShared` on a miss, retains only eligible non-strict results, and then returns the view.
A `CachedForLoad` retained hit has no remote manifest operation; a mutable-only drift clones the view around the shared decode, while a changed manifest causes a validation mismatch and rebuild.
`ForceFresh` always invokes `readManifestShared`, whose mandatory manifest `HEAD` re-proves body existence while a matching token can reuse the decode without a `GET` or re-decode.

Concurrent view construction for one `PartRefKey` shares one `readManifestShared` through `std::shared_future`; the cache mutex is never held across resolution, manifest read, or decode, and a leader exception reaches followers.

The method-routing contract uses `resolve(ForceFresh)` for mutable files and ref stamps, `getView(CachedForLoad)` for ordinary content, directories, storage objects, inline bytes, and blob plans, and `getView(ForceFresh)` for part-manifest export and write-source evidence.
`getStorageObjectsIfExist` is a dedicated one-lookup override that avoids the inherited `existsFile` plus `getStorageObjects` two-read path.

The in-flight transaction overlay remains above the facade; committed-source `createHardLink` and `moveFile` use `ForceFresh` access, while in-flight overlay reads may continue to use raw read-only `locate` calls.

Each level-1 facade mutation performs its underlying store or build operation and erases affected retained views only after success, except `dropRefBestEffort`, which erases even after swallowing a failure.
`publishEntries` is the shared sequence `startBuild -> adoptEvidence per entry -> stageManifest -> precommitAdd -> promoteBuild`.

`republishRef` uses a fresh source read; when the destination is already committed it compares content, re-syncs mutable files, and drops the source for equal content, while a different-content destination is a conflict.
The write ordering `precommitAdd`, blob validation, then `promote` is unchanged by the facade, and no cached view is used as write evidence or reachability state.

The wiring style rule forbids the tokens `->dropRef(`, `->updateRefPayload(`, `->dropNamespace(`, and `->promote(` outside `CachedPartFolderAccess.*`; `Core/` is exempt because it implements the protocol.
`decodePartManifest` rejects `path <= prev_path`; the encoder already emits sorted entries, and the strict ordering guarantee is what makes `PartFolderView` index-free.
`Store::lookupPath` and the manifest overload of `Store::listDirectory` are removed after callers migrate because pure tree queries do not belong in the protocol class.
The retained map is a `Common/CacheBase` LRU keyed by the canonical `PartRefKey` string and weighted by `estimatedBytes`; namespace erasure is a prefix scan and is hygiene rather than correctness.

The retained-view settings are `cas_part_folder_cache_bytes = 64 MiB`, `cas_part_folder_cache_max_entries = 10000`, and `cas_part_folder_cache_max_entry_bytes = 16 MiB`; zero bytes disables retention.
A retained view's weight is fixed overhead plus mutable key/value sizes plus `manifest_size`; views above `cas_part_folder_cache_max_entry_bytes` are served but not retained.

`shard_decode_cache` remains in `Cas::Store` with its TTL, `shard_write_seq`, and single-flight machinery, and `dedup_cache` remains there because neither should move into a new aggregate cache state.
The acceptance metric is `CasPartFolderManifestGets` no greater than the number of materialized load windows in controlled tests, rather than a server-wide inequality.
`explain(PartRefKey)` is structured diagnostic state containing retention status, the last decision, manifest reference, and estimated bytes, and is intended only for tests and log lines.
A view is published only after `readManifestShared` validates the body, and fill failures propagate as exceptions and are never cached.
Blob payload bytes are not cached; a committed view naming a missing blob still surfaces an exception when the payload is read.
Mutable files are not reachability state, and retained views hold no tokens with authority, do not affect GC in-degree, and do not protect objects from garbage collection.
Write-path source reads use `ForceFresh` and re-prove the manifest body with a mandatory `HEAD` on every call, so write evidence is never taken from a retained view.
The cache is process-local and non-durable, adds no TLA+ transition, and participates in neither publication nor reachability decisions.

The accepted residual delta is that an externally deleted or tampered manifest may go undetected on a validated `CachedForLoad` hit until eviction, mismatch, `ForceFresh`, or `StrictValidate`; write-evidence and strict paths retain immediate body liveness validation.
For suspected stale metadata, the operational kill switch is `cas_part_folder_cache_bytes = 0`; `fsck` and integrity probes should use `StrictValidate`, which never consults retained views.
Phase 5 byte-bounds `manifest_cache`, whose previous bound was 16384 entries with no byte limit and therefore had a multi-GB worst case when decoded manifests contained large inline bytes.

The byte-weighted manifest decode cache remains keyed by `(ManifestId, Token)`; a token mismatch causes a fresh `GET` and decode, a failed decode is not cached, and the mandatory manifest `HEAD` remains.

The rejected trust-until-invalidated generation-counter design would have depended on discovering every mutation site and a root-lease argument that does not cover pool-global shadow namespaces; validate-on-hit was chosen instead.

Serving a retained view for `ForceFresh` after only a matching ref resolve was rejected because ref currency does not prove manifest-body existence; `ForceFresh` therefore always performs the mandatory `HEAD` through `readManifestShared`.

A four-value `Freshness` enum was rejected because the mutable-read versus write-evidence distinction is carried by the method: mutable reads call `resolve`, while write-evidence reads call `getView(ForceFresh)`.
Materialized file and directory indexes were rejected because decoder-enforced canonical order makes binary search over the shared decode simpler and lighter.

Relocating `shard_decode_cache` and `dedup_cache` into a `CasCacheState` was rejected as unnecessary verified-machinery movement with regression risk; the memory goal is met by byte-bounding `manifest_cache` in Phase 5.
GC journal-only mutations do not route through the facade and do not invalidate retained views because they do not change committed refs or committed `RootRef::mutable_files`.
